title: Deruta ceramics
summary: Deruta in Umbria has painted tin-glazed maiolica since the Middle Ages, in ochre yellow, cobalt blue and copper green on a creamy white glaze. Here you throw a tazza, a wide dish on a foot, then paint its bands and the bird in the centre.
howToPlay: Look at the small tazza in the frame: that is the shape to make.
Drag across the spinning clay, row by row, to set the width of the dish and its foot; the lit outline shows the target.
Pick a colour from the swatches and tap a band to paint it like the target.
Press Check to see your stars.
rules: The tazza has twelve rows; each row can be set from narrow to wide.
Shape counts for most of the score, glaze for the rest.
Each band must carry the glaze shown on the target.
Undo takes back your last change; Reshape returns to the clay.
Three stars for a close shape with every band in the right glaze.
heritageNote: Deruta in Umbria, central Italy, has been a centre of maiolica since the thirteenth century. Its bowls, plates and footed dishes are painted in ochre, cobalt and copper green over a creamy white tin glaze, often with a bird, a portrait or a coat of arms at the centre, and workshops there still paint by hand.
